{
  "anomaly_detected": true,
  "confidence": 0.5,
  "anomalies": [
    {
      "category": "bridged_nets",
      "components": ["D30", "R60"],
      "pins": ["D30.2", "D30.4", "R60.1", "R60.2"],
      "nets": ["ESTOP_OUT", "Net-(D30-K2)"],
      "observed": "R60 pin 2 is on ESTOP_OUT, and D30 pin 4 (A2) is also on ESTOP_OUT. The LED2 path therefore runs from ESTOP_OUT through D30 and R60 back to ESTOP_OUT, so it carries no current and the LED can never light. The companion LED1 path (R59) returns to GND.",
      "expected": "By symmetry with R59 (K1 to GND), R60 should return the LED2 cathode to GND so that LED2 indicates ESTOP_OUT high.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"67\") (name \"ESTOP_OUT\") ... (node (ref \"D30\") (pin \"4\") (pinfunction \"A2\") ...) (node (ref \"J13\") (pin \"6\") ...) (node (ref \"R60\") (pin \"2\") (pintype \"passive\")) ..."},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"129\") (name \"Net-(D30-K2)\") ... (node (ref \"D30\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"K2\") ...) (node (ref \"R60\") (pin \"1\") ...)"},
        {"source": "spice", "quote": "R60 Net-_D30-K2_ ESTOP_OUT 130"}
      ],
      "impact": "The LED2 status indicator never illuminates. The e-stop output itself is not affected, but the diagnostic indication is lost.",
      "confidence": 0.5
    },
    {
      "category": "wrong_value",
      "components": ["R36"],
      "pins": ["R36.1", "R36.2"],
      "nets": ["VOUTN", "VOUTP"],
      "observed": "R36 is labelled value \"24k\", but its library description and MPN specify a 24 Ω part (\"24Ω 0805\", MPN FRC0805J240TSD, where the \"240\" code means 24 Ω). The value is off by a factor of 1000 relative to the part.",
      "expected": "The value field should match the selected part, which is 24 Ω. If a 24 kΩ bleed or balance resistor was intended, the MPN and description are wrong instead. Either way the BOM and schematic disagree.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(comp (ref \"R36\") (value \"24k\") ... (description \" 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(property (name \"MPN\") (value \"FRC0805J240TSD\"))"},
        {"source": "spice", "quote": "R36 VOUTN VOUTP 24k"}
      ],
      "impact": "If built as the MPN indicates, a 24 Ω resistor across the supercap output would draw a large load and bleed the bank very quickly, far beyond the intended design. If built as the value indicates, the BOM part is wrong.",
      "confidence": 0.4
    },
    {
      "category": "wrong_component_type",
      "components": ["Q1", "U6"],
      "pins": ["Q1.2", "Q1.3", "U6.1", "U6.6"],
      "nets": ["USBC_VBUS_IN", "+5V"],
      "observed": "Q1 (P-channel) has its source (pin 2) on +5V and its drain (pin 3) on USBC_VBUS_IN. The LTC4412 VIN pin is on USBC_VBUS_IN and its SENSE pin is on +5V. Every other P-channel high-side switch in the design (Q6, Q9) has its source on the input rail (+5V) and its drain on the load.",
      "expected": "For an ideal-diode OR-ing path from USB VBUS into +5V, the P-FET source should be at VBUS (the LTC4412 VIN) and its drain at the +5V output, with SENSE on the output side. The body diode of Q1 should conduct from VBUS toward +5V.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"206\") (name \"USBC_VBUS_IN\") ... (node (ref \"Q1\") (pin \"3\") (pinfunction \"D\") ...) (node (ref \"U6\") (pin \"1\") (pinfunction \"VIN\") ...)"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"2\") (name \"+5V\") ... (node (ref \"Q1\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"S\") ...) (node (ref \"U6\") (pin \"6\") (pinfunction \"SENSE\") ...)"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"Q6\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"S\") ...) (node (ref \"Q6\") (pin \"3\") (pinfunction \"D\") ...)"},
        {"source": "spec", "quote": "USB input \"OR-ing\"/protection circuitry (LTC4412 ideal-diode controller, U6)"}
      ],
      "impact": "With the FET source on the +5V output, the body diode blocks the intended VBUS-to-+5V direction and may conduct from the buck output back toward USB. The USB input path may not work or may back-feed the 5V rail.",
      "confidence": 0.3
    }
  ],
  "summary": "The netlist shows a likely mis-wired LED2 indicator (R60 returned to ESTOP_OUT, not GND) and an inconsistent R36 value (24k against a 24 Ω part), with a possibly reversed source/drain on the USB ideal-diode FET Q1. The evidence is circumstantial, and the spec documents several open issues that I did not report."
}

anomalies.observed: R60 pin 2 is on ESTOP_OUT, and D30 pin 4 (A2) is also on ESTOP_OUT. The LED2 path therefore runs from ESTOP_OUT through D30 and R60 back to ESTOP_OUT, so it carries no current and the LED can never light. The companion LED1 path (R59) returns to GND.
anomalies.expected: By symmetry with R59 (K1 to GND), R60 should return the LED2 cathode to GND so that LED2 indicates ESTOP_OUT high.
anomalies.impact: The LED2 status indicator never illuminates. The e-stop output itself is not affected, but the diagnostic indication is lost.

anomalies.observed: R36 is labelled value "24k", but its library description and MPN specify a 24 Ω part ("24Ω 0805", MPN FRC0805J240TSD, where the "240" code means 24 Ω). The value is off by a factor of 1000 relative to the part.
anomalies.expected: The value field should match the selected part, which is 24 Ω. If a 24 kΩ bleed or balance resistor was intended, the MPN and description are wrong instead. Either way the BOM and schematic disagree.

evidence.quote: (comp (ref "R36") (value "24k") ... (description " 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS")

anomalies.impact: If built as the MPN indicates, a 24 Ω resistor across the supercap output would draw a large load and bleed the bank very quickly, far beyond the intended design. If built as the value indicates, the BOM part is wrong.

anomalies.observed: Q1 (P-channel) has its source (pin 2) on +5V and its drain (pin 3) on USBC_VBUS_IN. The LTC4412 VIN pin is on USBC_VBUS_IN and its SENSE pin is on +5V. Every other P-channel high-side switch in the design (Q6, Q9) has its source on the input rail (+5V) and its drain on the load.
anomalies.expected: For an ideal-diode OR-ing path from USB VBUS into +5V, the P-FET source should be at VBUS (the LTC4412 VIN) and its drain at the +5V output, with SENSE on the output side. The body diode of Q1 should conduct from VBUS toward +5V.

evidence.quote: USB input "OR-ing"/protection circuitry (LTC4412 ideal-diode controller, U6)

anomalies.impact: With the FET source on the +5V output, the body diode blocks the intended VBUS-to-+5V direction and may conduct from the buck output back toward USB. The USB input path may not work or may back-feed the 5V rail.

parsed.summary: The netlist shows a likely mis-wired LED2 indicator (R60 returned to ESTOP_OUT, not GND) and an inconsistent R36 value (24k against a 24 Ω part), with a possibly reversed source/drain on the USB ideal-diode FET Q1. The evidence is circumstantial, and the spec documents several open issues that I did not report.
